**Design Critique: Portfolio Redesign**

**(1) Typography hierarchy: 4/5**
Strong size differentiation between the hero name (massive), subhead, and body text. The all-caps availability line and category tags create clear secondary tiers. Minor deduction: the "Featured Work" heading feels slightly underweighted relative to the hero's dominance.

**(2) Spacing consistency: 4/5**
Rhythmic vertical flow with generous breathing room between the CTA buttons and the work section. The grid gaps between portfolio cards appear uniform. Slight inconsistency in horizontal padding between the nav items and the main content container.

**(3) Color restraint: 5/5**
Exemplary discipline—deep navy background (#0f172a range) with a single accent blue (#3b82f6) reserved exclusively for interactive elements and semantic highlights. No competing gradients or rainbow chaos. The monochromatic supporting text prevents visual fatigue.

**(4) Contrast/readability: 4/5**
White-on-dark passes WCAG AA easily for large text. The light blue buttons maintain sufficient contrast against the navy. Minor concern: the "View Medoniq case" button's blue-on-blue relationship sits at the lower threshold of comfort; a slightly lighter fill or darker text would improve scanning.

**(5) Alignment/grid: 4/5**
Center-aligned hero creates appropriate focal gravity for a personal brand. The three-column portfolio grid demonstrates strict modular alignment. Nav bar shows solid left/right distribution. Deduction: the "N" badge in the bottom-left corner appears orphaned from any logical grid system.

**(6) Does design frame the work or upstage it? 5/5**
The dark "theater" background recedes effectively, allowing the colorful portfolio thumbnails (healthcare blues, TED reds, Avengers purples) to pop as the protagonists. The UI chrome is professional but deliberately understated—this is a frame, not a competitor.

---

**Verdict:**
This redesign successfully transforms what was likely a cluttered or amateurish "before" state into a polished, developer-designer hybrid aesthetic that signals technical competence. The fixes absolutely worked—the restrained palette and typographic clarity now let the actual case studies command attention rather than fighting with container noise.
